edition.authority: Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments
edition.notes: The official publication of the letter in the Congregation's own commentarii. The Latin preamble printed above the letter records that the Supreme Authority mandated the dispatch of the circular letters after consideration by this dicastery and by the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, and that the Italian version is to be held as the original from which the other translations were made. The dated protocol number is 467/05/L and the date given at the head of the letter is Roma, 17 ottobre 2006.
edition.publication: Notitiae 42 (2006), nn. 481-482, printed pp. 441-443, under the heading LITTERAE CIRCULARES
edition.title: Circular letter of 17 October 2006 as published in Notitiae 42 (2006) 441-443

passages.context: The complete letter was read. It records the July 2005 consultation of the conferences (Prot. N. 467/05/L of 9 July 2005); states at n. 1 that a text corresponding to pro multis has been the formula of the Roman Rite in Latin since the first centuries and that over the last thirty years some approved vernacular texts adopted the interpretative translation for all, per tutti or the like; affirms at n. 2 the validity of Masses celebrated with a duly approved formula equivalent to for all, citing the 1974 declaration of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith (AAS 66 [1974] 661), and that it is a dogma of faith that Christ died on the cross for all; gives at n. 3 six reasons for a more precise rendering, among them that the synoptic Gospels refer specifically to the many, that the Latin Roman Rite has always said pro multis and never pro omnibus in the consecration of the chalice, that the Eastern anaphoras contain the equivalent formula, that for all is rather an explanation belonging to catechesis, that for many remains open to including every human person while reflecting that salvation is not accomplished mechanically, and that under Liturgiam authenticam one should strive to remain more faithful to the Latin typical editions; and directs at n. 4 that conferences then using for all or its equivalent undertake the necessary catechesis of the faithful over the next one or two years so as to prepare them for the introduction of a precise vernacular rendering of pro multis in the next translation of the Roman Missal.
passages.notes: Read at the artifact pages. The letter's Italian is the original by its own preamble. This passage records what the letter directs and reasons; it is not a judgement about any particular vernacular text.

work.author: Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments
work.description: The circular letter of 17 October 2006, Prot. N. 467/05/L, sent by the Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments to the presidents of the episcopal conferences after consultation with the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith and on the directives of Benedict XVI, requiring that future vernacular translations of the Roman Missal render pro multis in the consecration of the chalice literally, and asking conferences then using for all or its equivalents to prepare the faithful by catechesis. The letter is in four numbered paragraphs; a Latin editorial preamble states that the Italian is to be held as the original.
work.title: Litterae circulares ad Praesides Conferentiarum Episcoporum de versione vernacula locutionis pro multis in formula consecrationis calicis
